details:
Q1: With `CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED=true`, what should happen when the routing data can't be verified? That covers a failed PR fetch or invalid JSON, empty `head.ref`, `head.repo.full_name` or `state`, a non-open PR, a fork head, or a head ref that isn't a valid branch name.
Choices:
A) Don't file the triage issue. Log `CHECK_TRIAGE skip reason=routing_unverified ...`, send a WARNING to Telegram, and exit 0 so a later re-run can retry. No unrouted issue is filed that would send the fix to the default branch. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Don't file the issue and exit non-zero with a CRITICAL alert, so the job fails visibly.
C) File the issue without an `Integration branch:` line (today's behaviour, so the fix routes to the default branch) and log a warning.
Q2: Should "mismatched data" also cover the failing check's head SHA differing from the PR's current `head.sha`, i.e. the branch moved after the check ran?
Choices:
A) Yes. Treat a SHA mismatch as unverified and handle it as chosen in Q1. The routed fix would otherwise target a branch whose tip the failing check never ran on. (RECOMMENDED)
B) No. Only check open state, same-repository head and a valid head ref; still route to the PR head branch after a later push.
